When your dog learns to understand this signal, you can start to use the signal multiple times without the physical touch. You can do this by slowly increasing the time before you use the physical action.

This will help your dog to feel more confident in his decision to sit, and he may even choose to sit on command. Step 4: Practice

But let me get something in the way of your feelings first:  The next time you think about why you feel guilt in a big way, ask yourself if your belief about that situation is accurate. If you have a clear reason to feel guilt, that’s OK.  But if you feel bad at all about it for no reason, think about whether it’s really justified.  I like to think of guilt like anger, if that makes sense.  Let’s say you feel guilty for not listening to your parents, but they didn’t want to get you help for your depression.  It’s okay to feel angry, but when you start seeing yourself to blame for things you didn’t really do, guilt is harder to get over.  
Sometimes guilt is like this overwhelming feeling of being not good enough - something like that, too.  That makes me remember something about my childhood: My mom was very hard on me, and when I think back on those times, I’m very careful to acknowledge that it felt OK to be hard on me.  So if you feel bad that you felt hard on yourself and now you’re guilty about it, think of it as your mom being hard on you.  How could you have handled it better?  
You also might feel guilty because you did something you regret and then felt bad about it.  If you ever find yourself doing that, focus on regret more than guilt.  The reason you regret it is usually that you did something to someone else, but instead of thinking more about the person you hurt, remember that maybe you didn’t choose to do it, and then when you think about it more later, you can let go of the guilt and recognize how you could’ve done better.

That fraction is called a “lull period” and it’s usually slower than any data transmission rate.  When you’re first entering an internet connection, that fraction can take anywhere from a few hundred milliseconds to half a second.   That’s why it’s a problem at times, for example when streaming video, where you need to know exactly how many bits you have to send down the wire.

Also, when you’re streaming video, it’s common for the video to start playing very slowly at first, then kind of ramp up speed in the middle and then slow down again and then ramp up again. With 4G, you have to stop an entire stream before starting again, which is what makes the playback lag so bad.  With 5G, the data connection doesn’t have to send out that fraction of the data until you actually need it, so you don’t experience the lag.  5G has also improved the overall reliability of data transmission for most applications.  4G was vulnerable to a phenomenon called “jitter” which occurs when lots of different parts of your internet connection move around a lot.
